source.title: Can Multilinguality benefit Non-autoregressive Machine Translation?
source.authors: Sweta Agrawal; Julia Kreutzer; Colin Cherry

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps model size and fits a relationship between translation BLEU and parameter count, testing downstream performance predictability with a different task and measure from language-model pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The scale experiment reports development BLEU against parameter count for AR and CTC translation models. It does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy, training tokens, compute, or compute-optimal allocation. Other BLEU results in the paper are not scale sweeps and are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains seven sizes of AR and CTC translation models from scratch and fits development BLEU against parameter count. That is a scale-versus-task-performance result in a new setting (multilingual MT, non-autoregressive). It is not a pretrained-LM loss result.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors fit BLEU against parameter count and find that the gap between CTC and AR grows with size. CTC plateaus at 26.7 versus 30.8 for AR, and the authors project that more NAR capacity alone will not reach AR quality. Their overall conclusion is that multilingual NAR is not yet ready: it suffers more negative transfer and gains less positive transfer than AR.
record.recipe_differences: Uses multilingual machine-translation models and development BLEU rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy; varies model size, not training tokens or compute. The fitted form is derived from prior neural machine-translation scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: Model family (AR versus CTC) and model size; the reported scale trends and plateaus differ between families.

fits_no_version.finding: CTC needs many more parameters than AR for comparable BLEU. The gap widens above about 10M parameters, and the projected curves suggest added NAR capacity alone will not reach AR quality.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling curves differ by decoding paradigm: non-autoregressive models saturate lower than autoregressive models at equal parameter count.

record.problems: The text gives no per-size BLEU values in the scale sweep, and the reported R2 for the second curve is unclear because the figure caption repeats R2 AR: 0.99. The authors also acknowledge that the comparison may be unfair because CTC and AR differ architecturally and AR may be limited by its teacher.

untested.parts: No pretraining held-out loss is reported; only BLEU versus parameters.
There is no check that a fit on small runs predicts larger runs. The 1B-parameter projection is an unverified extrapolation.
Tokens and compute are not varied, and no compute-optimal split is tested.
Depth and width co-vary with size (uniform scaling), so there is no fixed-parameter shape comparison.
A loss power law is not fitted in the MT regime. Only a composite BLEU form is fitted, so the power-law form itself is not tested.
No relation to pretraining loss is tested, and only one task (MT BLEU averaged over six pairs) is used. Scale range is about two orders of magnitude, from model dimension 128 to 1024.
No comparison of fitting choices or setups is made.

missing.what: Per-size development BLEU values and parameter counts for the seven AR and CTC models; the text gives them only graphically.
Fitted parameters a, b, c for each curve and the R2 for CTC (the caption duplicates the AR label).

record.verdict_notes: This is a weak, indirect bearing on V6. The models are supervised MT models trained from scratch, not pretrained LMs, so 'downstream' here means the training task's own quality metric. The plateaus are the fitted asymptote, not a breakdown of predictability, so the record's limits_scope label is dropped. The authors acknowledge the AR/CTC comparison may be unfair because of architecture differences and teacher limits. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
It does not test whether small-run fits predict held-out loss in much larger language-model runs.
No fixed-compute allocation between model parameters and training tokens is tested.
The study does not compare architectural details at fixed parameter count.
Although this is a different training setting, it does not test whether the claimed held-out-loss power law transfers to other modalities or regimes.
Tests development BLEU for machine translation versus parameter count, not a range of downstream tasks or performance versus pretraining loss.
The study does not compare fitting choices or setups to determine whether exponents or compute-optimal splits depend on them.

rows.subject: AR models
rows.stage_stated: trained on distilled datasets from bilingual AR-big teacher
rows.operation_detail: Uniformly scaled model capacity and fitted development BLEU as a function of parameter count.

conditions.value: Development BLEU averaged across six language pairs

rows.measure: Development BLEU versus number of parameters
rows.value: The fitted scaling-law model is described as almost perfectly describing the relationship; R2 AR: 0.99. AR models plateau at BLEU 30.8.
rows.note: The paper says AR and CTC outputs are approximately similar below 10M parameters, with the BLEU gap increasing as parameter count rises. The figure caption prints R2 AR: 0.99 for both curves; the text explicitly assigns R2 AR: 0.99 to AR. The stated plateau qualifies the scale trend.
rows.check: State should be observed, not partial. The fitted form BLEU(N) ≈ a·exp(-b(1/N)^c) has a built-in ceiling, so the plateau at 30.8 is part of the predicted curve, not a deviation. The text reports R2 0.99 for AR. Per-size BLEU values and parameter counts appear only in Figure 3.

rows.subject: CTC models
rows.stage_stated: trained on distilled datasets from bilingual AR-big teacher
rows.operation_detail: Uniformly scaled model capacity and fitted development BLEU as a function of parameter count.

conditions.value: Development BLEU averaged across six language pairs

rows.measure: Development BLEU versus number of parameters
rows.value: The fitted scaling-law model is described as almost perfectly describing the relationship; CTC plateaus early at BLEU 26.7. Extrapolating the curves to 1 billion parameters, the authors state that increasing CTC capacity is insufficient to reach AR quality.
rows.note: The figure caption prints R2 AR: 0.99 for both curves, so the R2 attribution for CTC is unclear. The early plateau and persistent gap to AR qualify the scale trend.
rows.check: State should be observed. The text says the fit almost perfectly describes the curves, and CTC's plateau at 26.7 is the fitted ceiling. The CTC-versus-AR gap bears on NAR capacity, not on whether BLEU is predictable from scale. CTC's R2 is unreadable because the caption prints 'R2 AR: 0.99' twice.

relationships.condition: AR and CTC multilingual En→X translation models, seven sizes trained on AR-big distilled data
relationships.reason: Development BLEU follows the fitted scale curve closely: AR R2 0.99, and the authors describe the fit as almost perfect for both (r1, r2). Evidence is in-sample fit only, with no held-out extrapolation check.
relationships.display_finding: Development BLEU closely matched scaling curves for both architectures, with AR R² of 0.99, but extrapolation to held-out sizes was untested.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
